bull.b: Demonstrated proteoform resolution and substantially higher reproducibility could give Nautilus a differentiated position in proteomics research. If validated across additional assays, this capability may support customer adoption, strengthen scientific credibility, and underpin recurring instrument and consumable demand.

The shift toward proteoforms is supported by a defined product roadmap, increased staffing, and multiple planned assays. A broader assay menu can improve platform utility, support repeat customer usage, and create a more credible foundation for eventual instrument, consumable, and software revenue.

Lower operating expenses and improved net loss demonstrate management is controlling spending while continuing platform development. Sustained discipline can extend financial flexibility, preserve resources for priority proteoform programs, and reduce the pace at which commercialization efforts consume capital.

bear.b: Revenue remains extremely small relative to the company’s operating cost base, showing that commercialization has not yet reached meaningful scale. This leaves Nautilus dependent on future product adoption and successful execution before recurring instrument, consumable, and service revenue can support the business.

Nautilus continues to consume substantial cash while management anticipates additional fundraising, and the new equity facility creates a mechanism for future share issuance. Capital access may support development, but financing needs can increase dilution risk and constrain strategic flexibility if commercialization is delayed.

The broadscale delay postpones a potentially important application area and extends the period before the platform can address a wider customer market. Continued probe, model, and architecture work increases execution uncertainty and may defer broader instrument placements, assay revenue, and customer expansion.
